caption: An ice cube is flicked onto a hot skillet, and it skitters around and shrinks as it melts.

sa.check: An ice cube is flicked onto the skillet.
The cube slides about on the surface.
Steam or a wet film shows at the cube's edge.
The flick comes first and the sliding and shrinking follow.

pc.expect: The cube only shrinks and rounds off while it is on the hot pan.
pc.fail: The cube grows; or regains a sharp corner; or freezes into a clear block again; or alternates between smaller and larger.

pc.expect: The cube glides and spins because it was flicked and because it rides on its own steam; its path bends only where it meets the pan's slope or wall.
pc.fail: The cube darts off at a new angle with nothing touching it and no wall met; or stops dead and sets off again from rest; or climbs the pan's wall and hangs there; or moves against the flick before touching anything.

pc.expect: The cube turns only into water and steam, and the shrinking cube is the cube that was flicked.
pc.fail: The cube vanishes in a single frame while still large; or a second cube appears; or the cube splits into pieces that are each as big as the cube was; or water appears far across the pan with no cube reaching there.

pc.expect: The cube stays a hard solid that skids without deforming, and the melt it leaves is a thin film lying on the pan's surface.
pc.fail: The cube smears like butter as it slides; or flattens into a pancake; or the melt stands as a dome on the pan; or the cube bounces off the pan like a ball.

pc.expect: The cube stays on top of the pan's surface and nothing passes through the pan.
pc.fail: The cube sinks into the pan's metal; or passes through the pan's wall; or the pan changes shape; or the cube passes through the pan's handle.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The skillet's finish and the hob around it stay the same.
pc.fail: The skillet changes colour; or its handle changes shape; or items around the hob rearrange.
